query: What signals in a travel-expense description predict whether it will be declined?

per_column.name: description_specificity
per_column.rationale: Directly derived from the description text (the query's focus signal), with three clean, interpretable buckets that can be cross-tabbed against decline rate. Well-separated categories.

per_column.name: expense_purpose
per_column.rationale: Interpretable purpose categories inferred from the description; strong associational variable for segmenting decline rates, with reasonable category balance.

per_column.name: source_id_present
per_column.rationale: Clean binary flag with a decent split (327/173) that can be compared against decline; captures provenance/completeness signal without restating the focus.

per_column.name: entry_origin
per_column.rationale: Manual vs auto-generated origin is an interpretable, well-separated segmentation plausibly associated with decline rate.

per_column.name: ci_vendor
per_column.rationale: Vendor categories are interpretable and groupable; a reasonable external axis to compare against decline, though some low-frequency tail categories.

per_column.name: department_group
per_column.rationale: Interpretable organizational segmentation with well-populated categories; classic axis for comparing decline rates across departments.

per_column.name: asset_category
per_column.rationale: Clear, well-separated category axis (hardware/travel/cloud/etc.) suitable for grouped comparison against decline.

per_column.name: processed_date_present
per_column.rationale: Binary presence flag with balanced split (295/205); interpretable and comparable, though may partly proxy processing state rather than being fully independent of outcome.

per_column.name: ci_hardware_class
per_column.rationale: Interpretable hardware-type segmentation; usable despite a large NULL segment (152), which itself forms a comparable group.

judge.rationale: As a set, the columns provide multiple external, interpretable axes (description specificity, purpose, provenance flags, entry origin, vendor, department, asset/hardware category) that a human can group on and cross-tabulate against decline rate. Categories are well-separated with human-readable labels rather than opaque scores, satisfying the EDA claim. None merely restates state_declined. Minor deductions: processed_date_present may be partly downstream of the outcome (potential leakage into the decline relationship), and several columns carry sizable NULL or long low-frequency tails; but overall the set supports discovering meaningful, interpretable relationships.
